reuse.why: It extends the shared getScheduledAmount helper, but re-implements the 7.5% tolerance inline (Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075)) instead of calling the existing getApproxNumberThreshold in shared/rules.ts.

duplication.why: The approximate-tolerance formula is a second copy of getApproxNumberThreshold, so the matching tolerance and the planning tolerance can drift apart.

placement.why: The rule is added to the shared expected-amount helper in shared/schedules.ts where it belongs, with server call sites passing the op.

scope.why: Only the helper, its server/API call sites, comments and tests are touched.

maintainability.why: A trailing op parameter after the boolean inverse forces callers to write getScheduledAmount(x, false, op), the tolerance constant is duplicated, and several callers (budget schedule template, client balance/list views) still ignore the op.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount: inline 0.075 tolerance instead of getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.ts

disguised_duplication.where: the approximate branch reshapes getApproxNumberThreshold's Math.round(Math.abs(n) * 0.075) into amount + Math.sign(amount) * ... rather than calling it

one_place.where: The rule lands in getScheduledAmount, but server/budget/schedule-template.ts still computes its own schedule amount (midpoint, no approximate handling) and the client callers (Balance.tsx, SchedulesTable.tsx, SchedulesListItem.tsx, MobileSchedulesPage.tsx, useScheduleEdit.ts) call it without the op, so they do not apply the approximate rule
